correctness.rationale: The partial transpose decomposes into two positive singleton entries and three explicit 2-by-2 blocks. Exact eigenvalue formulas reduce negativity to a three-variable expression. For fixed y, strict convexity forces x=z; the reduced one-variable function decreases on [0,1/3] and increases on [1/3,1], giving the unique uniform minimizer, exact value (sqrt(5)-1)/6, and inertia (5,1,2).

value.rationale: The exact minimum quantifies a robustness floor inside a natural NPT-subspace simplex, rather than merely restating NPT existence. The unique minimizer occurs exactly on an inertia-transition boundary, showing that minimizing negativity magnitude and maximizing negative-eigenvalue count are structurally different. The 2-by-4 three-generator case is the first nontrivial diagonal simplex where this phenomenon can be stated as a complete exact minimization.
